self.title: Cycle 56 · Synthesis of Operational Memory Foundations

detail.title: Synthesis of Operational Memory Foundations
detail.summary: This cycle completes the systematic revision of three core notebooks focusing on the thermodynamic and operational costs of memory. We integrate findings on coarse-graining, non-equilibrium driven dynamics, and passive degree-of-freedom coupling. Key insights identify that persistent physical states only function as effective memory when they demonstrably reduce future uncertainty or dissipation, a condition constrained by the resolution of the observer's model.

detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory
detail.question: When does a persistent physical state function as memory by improving predictions or altering future control?
detail.reason: Previous revisions established the dependency on coarse-graining; the next logical step is to bridge the reconstruction accuracy with energy dissipation.

detail.title: Information Engines and Thermodynamic Dissipation
detail.question: How do temporal correlations and memory states govern work production and dissipation in information engines?
detail.reason: Current findings establish upper bounds; finite-lifetime impacts remain an open operational constraint.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.question: How do energy costs scale with reliability and retention time in physical memory systems?
detail.reason: Foundations are set; formalizing the scaling relations is required.

detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory (Revised)
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes the criteria for causal memory, establishing that a persistent state only functions as memory when it provides predictive sufficiency or control utility relative to a specific coarse-grained model. Physical memory systems are bounded by the information-theoretic cost of maintaining these states against dissipation, with non-driven passive degrees of freedom modifying the effective entropy production rate.
detail.reason: Integrating new findings on coarse-graining and Langevin dynamics refines the operational criteria.

detail.title: Thermodynamics and Nonreciprocal Information Engines
detail.summary: We find that non-reciprocal couplings and non-driven passive degrees of freedom significantly alter the entropy production bounds of information engines. Predictive power is bounded by the ability of the system to maintain causal states, where dissipation is minimized when state transitions align with the driven dynamics.
detail.reason: Refining the role of non-driven degrees of freedom provides a more accurate view of dissipation bounds.
